title: Compact Triage Conductor: lightweight admin task orchestration and conversation-history stitching
creator: Jordan Matthews
description: Build a compact orchestration layer that transforms curated runbook steps into lightweight executable tasks (Compact Triage Conductor). Goals: enable first-line support to run idempotent admin utilities from the Console, stitch short conversation histories for context-aware automation, and emit structured telemetry and audit entries for each task execution.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console shows a 'Triage' action card with up to 6 curated steps for a common incident class and a single-click 'Run as Task' flow
2) Each step executes as an idempotent task with typed inputs and returns structured result objects stored in audit-log for 90 days
3) Conversation history (last 10 messages) is attached to the task context and made available to the executor runtime without leaking PII by default
4) Automated fallback: if a step fails (non-idempotent or permission error), the flow surfaces a suggested rollback and logs a decision trace to the incident dashboard
5) End-to-end integration tests + test dataset (3 synthetic incidents) pass in CI and a canary rollout to prod-dedicated infra is configured
comments: 2025-01-22 - Kickoff: scoped to 'access-reset', 'cache-flush', 'route-failover' playbooks first. Decided to keep runtime surface minimal: HTTP task API + signed ephemeral tokens for Console-to-runtime calls.
2025-01-28 - Design sync with UX: 'compact' card needs to render step inputs inline; PM asked for >= 80% success rate in benign dryruns before wider rollout.

2025-01-30 - Security review onboarding: discussed PII stripping heuristics. Trade-off: removing too much context reduces triage success; compromise: configurable retention per-project with default redact=true. See confluence: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/OPS/Compact+Triage+Conductor

2025-02-03 - Eng review: chosen pattern is TaskDef (yaml) + small runner in ops-runtime. Pros: simple, fast to implement. Cons: another DSL to support. Action: implement a strict type-checker and keep DSL surface subset of existing runlet grammar.

2025-02-07 - PR opened for runner shim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/839 (WIP). Initial smoke tests show task execution latency median 210ms on smallest dedicated instance—within SLO.

2025-02-10 - UX feedback from support beta: suggested step grouping and pre-filled inputs from incident template. We added 'prefill' mapping in TaskDef and a mapping prototype in drive: https://drive.google.com/compact-triage/prototype
2025-02-12 - Blocking note: IAM integration for ephemeral tokens needs a minor API change in auth service (ENG-271443). Added as dependency; blocker until API deploys to staging.
notes: Implementation choices: use KV-backed ephemeral context store (90s TTL) vs embedding context in signed token. We chose KV store to avoid token size blowups and to enable redaction. Telemetry events will follow the existing admin-telemetry schema. Logged audit entries must be queryable by incident ID and operator ID.
next_steps: Finish auth API change (ENG-271443) and deploy to staging
Merge runner shim PR and add e2e tests with synthetic incidents
Instrument canary rollout (5% traffic to dedicated) and monitor success/failure rates
Productize prefill mapping and ship small Console UX tweak
